To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beam dynamics of the FERI@ELETTRA Linac is well understood, that the beam quality is preserved along the machine and that the BBU instability is the most important issue to be tackled.
the FEL bandwidth is mainly limited by the energy chirp and that the beam breakup instability is the main source of the emittance dilution.
the beam emittance and the energy spread can be preserved within the desired values, and the beam quality is not degraded in the presence of wakefields and the BBU instability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the beam dynamics in the FEL, in order to maximize the FEL bandwidth and the efficiency of the amplification process.
the design of the Fermi linac in order to optimize the electron beam dynamics for a seeded FEL.
the optimization of the electron beam dynamics in view of the FEL performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of the Fermi Linacs is a very challenging task, and the beam dynamics is a very important aspect of it.
the beam dynamics in Fermi is well under control, with the exception of some specific issues that need to be further investigated.
, in principle, the FEL project at Fermi can be realized, and that the main issues have already been identified and addressed in a satisfactory way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FEL project at Elettra is feasible, and it will be possible to reach the design goals of a 1.4 GeV, 1.5 mm rms emittance, 0.5% rms energy spread, 0.1 mrad normalized rms beam divergence electron beam.
we have been able to design an electron beam with a small emittance and energy spread, which is suitable for the generation of a high quality FEL radiation in the far infrared range.

we have developed a robust design of the FEL, able to provide the required performance in terms of bandwidth and output power, and we have also developed a reliable method to correct the beam dynamics effects that may cause an undesired emittance growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BBU instability can be tamed by using a proper combination of the available techniques, and the emittance dilution is limited to a small value, even in the presence of the wakefields.

, with the use of a suitable correction scheme, the BBU instability can be suppressed and the final beam emittance can be preserved below 1 nm, which represents the threshold for a successful operation of the FEL.
a careful beam dynamics design is mandatory for a successful operation of a seeded FEL.
